enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
522 AM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 520 AM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

 - Mostly dry, breezy, with seasonable temperatures today through
   Thursday.

 - Cold blast of air with windy conditions Thursday evening and
   Friday morning as cold front moves through. Well below normal 
   temperatures for Friday and the weekend.

 - In addition to the winds on Friday we will see a chance for
   lowland rain showers and high elevation rain/snow mix. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1033 PM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026

We will have a nice couple of days, but it is looking more and
more likely that we will see a big changes to our weather by the 
end of the week. Currently our region remains sandwiched between 
an upper level trough over the Great Basin and an upper level 
ridge over the Gulf coast. Many times a pattern like this would 
draw up moisture, but for this time we are moving in drier air. 
Some of the moisture associated with what is left of Hurricane 
Simon, will be drawn up to our east (though just to our east). 
Most of the area will stay dry on Tuesday and Wednesday, with the 
one exception being Hudspeth county which will have a slight 
chance for rain both afternoons, as it is closer to some of that 
tropical moisture. Temperatures both Tuesday and Wednesday will 
run a few degrees above average east of the Rio Grande and a few 
degrees below averages west of river. 

On Thursday our weather starts to change. The upper level trough
that was to our northwest, will push east, but a chunk of energy
will carve and form a new upper level trough which will retrograde
back to our southwest. At the surface a strong back door cold 
front will approach the region from the east. This cold front will
bring strong surface winds and dramatically colder air. High 
temperature on Thursday will be similar to Tuesday and Wednesday, 
but high temperatures on Friday will be 10 to 15 degrees cooler. 
As the cold front pushes west Thursday night we will see a band 
of strong winds push across the area. Wind gusts in excess to 50 
mph will be possible, especially for locations just to the west of
area mountains. The strong gusty winds will slowly come down on 
Friday, but most of Friday will be cool with those brisk east 
winds. The upper level trough to our southwest will try and lift 
some of the moisture up over the cold front which will give lots 
of clouds and could give us a some precipitation both Friday and
Saturday. The extended deterministic GFS keeps most of the rain 
just south of the area, but the extended deterministic EC brings 
a good area of rain and maybe a mix of rain and snow (yes I said 
snow) to the highest elevations of the Sacramento Mountains. If 
the EC model is right, Friday will be a wet, cold and dreary day, 
if the GFS is correct is will be cool and brisk. Either way it 
will certainly finally feel like Fall.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 520 AM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

VFR conditions expected through the period with SCT080 SCT250.
After 18Z...SCT080 occasionally becomes BKN080 and over the Gila
region, a slight chance of BKN060 -SHRA until 23Z. Surface winds
variable AOB 7 knots this morning, increasing to southwest
10-15G25 knots after 18Z. Winds then becoming west 7-10 knots
after 03Z.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 520 AM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Typical Fall weather through Thursday with sunshine and seasonable
temperatures. Breezy afternoons today and Wednesday, but min RHs 
remain well above critical levels. Strong cold front sweeps in 
from the east early Thursday evening, reaching the Arizona state 
line by Friday morning. Gusty east winds of 35-55 mph through 
Friday morning before weakening some late Friday. The strongest 
gusts will be adjacent to the Intl Border and west slopes of 
terrain. Some showers with this, and a brief mix of rain and snow 
is possible at the highest elevations of the Sacramento Mtns 
Friday morning. Temperatures will be well below normal Friday 
through the weekend.

Min RH: Lowlands 20-30% through Thursday, increasing to 30-45%
Friday and Saturday. Mountains 25-40% through Thursday, 
increasing to 45-60% Friday and Saturday. Vent rates good-very
good today and Wednesday, becoming fair-good Thursday and Friday.
